conviction_note: The P&L is already public - revenue GBP143m, adj operating profit c.GBP15.8m, margin 11.1%, net debt GBP69.6m, FY26 >GBP40m, FY27 above consensus were all pre-announced on 28 July - so tomorrow carries almost no headline surprise and the reaction is a function of one thing: the first quantification of the Demand Flexibility regulated haircut that actually caused the -11.76% on 28 July. The English wire copy misattributed that fall to margins (which rose 10bp); the RNS paragraph naming the cause is the unread part. Net of a fat new-CEO tail and a +9.3% five-day run-up, I get +1.4, which is a probability-weighted centre and NOT a forecast of a small move - this name's median absolute print move is 4.02% with a fat tail either way (+13.86%, -11.76% both inside two years).

findings.finding: The -11.76% on 28 July was not a margin miss - margin ROSE to 11.1% from 11.0% - it was one unquantified paragraph: 'changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half.' Demand Flexibility sits inside Energy Transition, which RBC sizes at ~11% of group sales but MORE THAN 20% of earnings, so the market de-rated ~20% of earnings on an unsized regulatory haircut. Tomorrow is the first disclosure with two months of post-change trading behind it, and the company has already twice said the change is 'consistent with the Board's expectations' while upgrading FY27 in the same announcement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance upgrades at LUCE have been paid: FY25 full-year TU 2026-01-29 +7.09%, FY25 results with the FY26 >GBP37m guide 2026-03-25 +8.40%, Q1 upgrade to >GBP40m 2026-05-19 +2.13%. The single exception is 2026-07-28, where an FY27 upgrade came attached to this new structural caveat and the stock fell 11.76%. Both prior interim results prints were positive: 2024-09-10 +2.35%, 2025-09-09 +9.46%. Across all 17 observed prints the mean is +2.53% and 10 of 17 are positive.
findings.original_quote: As expected, changes to the regulated mechanics of Demand Flexibility have begun to crystallise, and are expected to reduce recurring revenue per EV charger towards a more sustainable level early in the second half. Such changes are consistent with the Board's expectations and, as a result, the Board continues to expect Adjusted Operating Profit for 2026 to exceed GBP40m
findings.why_not_priced: The attribution is wrong in the coverage the marginal buyer reads. RTT News reported the fall with no explanation at all ('the article offers no analysis or commentary about the reason behind the share price drop'); MarketBeat's instant alert attributed it to 'the modest margin improvement... appears to have disappointed investors', which is factually backwards since the margin rose 10bp and the company said so in the same bullet. If the market had the right model of what tomorrow resolves, you would not see five analysts all constructive (RBC Buy 320p, Deutsche Bank upgrading to Buy 270p on 8 September explicitly to preview this print, average target 289p) while the stock sits 8% below its pre-update level - you would see targets cut to reflect a sized haircut. Nobody has sized it publicly because the company has not yet given the number.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 trading update of 19 May 2026 contains no mention of any regulatory change and instead says 'Demand Flexibility revenues from EV chargers increased significantly during the quarter', confirming the 28 July paragraph was genuinely new information rather than a restatement - https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/luceco--luce/q1-2026-trading-update/9574200

findings.finding: The one P&L line NOT pre-announced is adjusted PBT / adjusted EPS, and it should show a step change in optics. In H1 2025 adjusted operating profit rose 9.5% but adjusted PBT FELL 3.6% and adjusted EPS rose only 3.5%, because bank net debt had ballooned 72.6% YoY (GBP39.4m to GBP68.0m) on acquisitions and the interest charge was ~GBP3.0m. In H1 2026 net debt is flat YoY at GBP69.6m against GBP68.0m, so that step-up has annualised and UK rates have fallen. On a flat ~GBP3.0-3.1m finance charge, c.GBP15.8m of adjusted operating profit implies adjusted PBT of ~GBP12.7m (+17.6%) and adjusted EPS of ~6.8p (+15%) against last year's +3.5% - the earnings line growing FASTER than the pre-announced operating line, which is the reverse of last year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025 interims printed adjusted EPS +3.5% against adjusted operating profit +9.5% - the weakest EPS/EBIT gap in the record - and the stock still rose 9.46%, so this shareholder base is not punitive on the EPS line. There is no instance in the 17-event record of the EPS line itself being the stated driver of a move.
findings.original_quote: Adjusted operating profit 13.8 | 12.6 | +9.5% ... Adjusted profit before tax 10.8 | 11.2 | -3.6% ... Adjusted basic earnings per share 5.9p | 5.7p | +3.5% ... Bank net debt 68.0 | 39.4 | +72.6%
findings.why_not_priced: Every piece of wire copy and every broker summary I found quotes the pre-announced operating profit ('+14%') and none carries a PBT or EPS figure, because the trading update does not give one. The market's anchor for this print is therefore an EBIT number; the EPS number is the one that lands tomorrow and it is arithmetically better than the anchor. If this were priced you would see previews quoting an H1 EPS estimate - Deutsche Bank's 8 September preview, as reported, quotes revenue and divisional growth only. My PBT/EPS figures are MY estimate from two primary documents, clearly labelled, not a company number.
findings.independence: Corroborated by the FY25 results RNS, which shows the same mechanism reversing over a full year once the debt annualised: adjusted operating profit +16.6% but adjusted EPS +20.0% - https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/luceco--luce/2025-full-year-results/9490302

findings.finding: The FY26 guide of >GBP40m requires H2 adjusted operating profit of at least GBP24.2m against GBP20.0m in H2 2025 - +21% YoY, ACCELERATING from the +14.5% just delivered in H1 - and it has to be delivered in the very half the Demand Flexibility revenue-per-charger haircut lands in. In the same half, H1 drop-through was poor: my decomposition of the disclosed 'c.120%' Energy Transition growth and 'c.6%' core growth puts Energy Transition revenue at ~GBP18.2m from ~GBP8.3m, i.e. ~GBP9.9m of incremental revenue in a supposedly high-margin stream, for only GBP2.0m of incremental group profit and 10bp of margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only time an H2-weighting question was live at a LUCE print was the 2025 interims, where the company said 'firmly on track to deliver full year expectations with a strong order book entering H2' and the stock rose 9.46% - the market took the reassurance rather than doing the arithmetic. H2 weighting is also normal here: H2 was 59% of FY25 operating profit and 57% of FY24, against the 60.5% FY26 implies, so this is a stretch and not an outlier.
findings.why_not_priced: The H2 bridge needs two documents that are six months apart - the FY25 results for the GBP33.8m full-year and GBP13.8m H1 comparator, and the July update for the GBP15.8m and the >GBP40m guide - and no piece of coverage I found subtracts them. But I am sizing this SMALL and not large for two reasons the lessons file names: it agrees with a short seller who is already building, so it is likely in the price; and the revenue decomposition rests on two rounded percentages ('c.120%', 'c.6%') and is fragile to a point either way.
findings.independence: The same RNS supplies the inventory build that CORROBORATES rather than contradicts the ramp - 'Bank Net Debt... increased slightly to GBP69.6m... reflecting an investment in inventory ahead of the second half' - so the company has put stock behind the H2 it is guiding to. Shares a document with the net-debt finding below; see that finding's independence note. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/luceco--luce/h1-2026-trading-update/9689898

findings.finding: Dr Thorsten Muller became CEO on 1 September 2026, three weeks before this print, succeeding founder John Hornby after 21 years. He did not set the FY26 >GBP40m or the FY27 'ahead of consensus' guidance - both were given on 28 July while Hornby was on sabbatical and while the board was still 'in advanced discussions with a number of candidates'. This is his first results statement and the first opportunity to rebase numbers he does not own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this name - Hornby ran it for the whole 17-event record, so there is no observation of how this shareholder base reacts to a CEO transition here. The CEO Retirement RNS (2026-06-15) and the Appointment RNS (2026-08-10) were both non-events for the tape: the stock closed 225p on 10 August against 226p on 7 August. That the appointment itself was a non-event is why the first-results risk is still live rather than already discharged.
findings.original_quote: Appointment of Dr Thorsten Muller as CEO
findings.why_not_priced: It is a known fact with an unknown consequence, and the sell-side has priced the fact and not the consequence - Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy on 8 September, a week after Muller started, on divisional growth forecasts that assume the inherited guidance holds. If the market were pricing reset risk you would expect the shares to have drifted DOWN into a new CEO's first print rather than up 9.3% in five sessions. I hold this as a fat left tail rather than a central case: three weeks is too short to kitchen-sink a half that was already pre-announced under the previous regime, and a strategic reset at a UK small cap normally waits for full-year results or a capital markets day.
findings.independence: The departing founder-CEO sold 505,000 shares at 224.06p (~GBP1.13m) on 21 August 2026, two days before the 30-day closed period for a 22 September interim announcement would have begun - a timing detail visible only in the RNS, which points the same way on incentives - https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/luceco--luce/director-pdmr-shareholding/9737201

findings.finding: Bank net debt rose GBP17.3m in the half - from GBP52.3m at 31 December 2025 to GBP69.6m at 30 June 2026 - against a GBP0.6m FALL over the equivalent half of 2025. The 28 July RNS framed it only against the prior-year half-end ('increased slightly to GBP69.6m (H1 2025: GBP68.0m)'), which is the comparison that makes a GBP17.3m six-month build read as GBP1.6m. Tomorrow's cash flow statement and net debt bridge make it explicit, and adjusted free cash flow should land roughly GBP10m+ worse than the GBP10.3m of H1 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Decisive, and it is why this is sized at -0.4 and not -1.5: at the 2025 interims bank net debt printed +72.6% YoY (GBP39.4m to GBP68.0m) and the stock rose 9.46% on the day. This shareholder base has demonstrably looked straight through a far larger balance-sheet expansion at this exact event. The FY24-to-FY25 pattern also shows the working capital reversing - adjusted free cash flow GBP3.5m in 2024 then GBP30.4m in 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: Every summary of the July update I read - the AI abstract on Investegate, the Kalkine and Financial-News write-ups, the Investing.com piece - repeats the company's own YoY framing and none compares the GBP69.6m to the GBP52.3m the company itself published in March. But the lessons file is explicit that financing is a question, not a verdict, and the answer here is benign: the company says the money bought 'an investment in inventory ahead of the second half', and the H2 the guidance requires is exactly the ramp that inventory would serve. So this is an optic on the day, not a solvency point - leverage still fell to 1.5x, inside the 1-2x target range.
findings.independence: Shares the 28 July RNS with the H2-ramp finding above; the GBP52.3m comparator comes from a different document (the FY25 results RNS, 2026-03-25). The two findings are NOT independent of each other and point opposite ways on the same inventory build - the H2-ramp finding treats it as an unmet requirement, this one treats it as a cash cost, and the inventory itself is the reason both are sized small.

findings.finding: The stock closed 235.0p on 21 September, up 4.91% on the day against the FTSE 250's +1.18%, on 414,767 shares versus a September median of ~226k - roughly 3.7 points of idiosyncratic move on 1.8x normal volume, the session before a print, with no RNS from the company since 24 August. Over five sessions it is +9.3% (215p on 14 September). Anticipatory buying, at least partly domestic retail: SQC Research published a buy note on 17 September at 220p with a 275p target saying the results 'will be good and could show that the next year will be better than market expectations'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is why the penalty is only -0.4. Measured on LUCE's own 17 prints, the 5-day run-up into the event has NO predictive power for the reaction: Spearman +0.096, and the five events with a >3% run-up averaged +4.43% against +1.75% for the other twelve - i.e. on this name a run-up has historically preceded BETTER prints, not worse. The one cautionary precedent is 2024-01-30, the largest run-up in the sample at +9.70%, which printed -4.76%. The current +9.3% is the second-largest.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not 'unpriced' - it IS the price, and I am carrying it as a debit against the other findings rather than as information. What it tells me is that some of the relief trade in finding 1 has already been taken, which is exactly what should be visible if my central thesis were becoming consensus. I looked for a company-specific cause for the 21 September move and found none: the Investegate RNS history shows nothing since the 24 August PDMR notification, and the Deutsche Bank upgrade that plausibly caused the 8 September +4.0% is two weeks old and was fully retraced by 14 September.
findings.independence: The FTSE 250 comparison is a second, independent series - https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5EFTMC?range=10d&interval=1d - and confirms the move is idiosyncratic rather than market beta.

outside_window.finding: Q3 2026 trading update on 27 October 2026 is the first release covering a FULL quarter under the changed Demand Flexibility mechanics, and is therefore the real test of the FY26 >GBP40m and FY27 'ahead of consensus' guidance rather than tomorrow's half-year statement.

Dr Thorsten Muller's strategic review of the group, if there is one, would conventionally land at the FY26 results in March 2027 or a capital markets day, not at a half-year statement three weeks into the job - so the larger part of the new-CEO reset risk sits outside this window.

searched_and_found_nothing: No Ofgem, NESO or Elexon decision published between 28 July and 21 September 2026 that quantifies the change to Demand Flexibility revenue per EV charger. Searched Ofgem decisions, NESO's DFS pages, the Balancing and Settlement Code modification register and the GOV.UK clean flexibility roadmap (July 2026 update). The nearest dated items are Ofgem's approval of the evolved DFS design on 2026-03-25 and a stated intention to update on demand-connection flexibility measures in 'Autumn 2026' - neither sizes Luceco's per-charger economics. This is the single biggest hole in this hunt: the magnitude of the haircut is the price-sensitive number and it is not publicly available ahead of the print.

No company-specific cause found for the +4.91% on 2026-09-21. Investegate's LUCE history shows no RNS since 24 August 2026; no broker action, trade-press item or sector read-across surfaced for that date.
Investegate's UK short-positions page returned no LUCECO row when queried, so the FCA files are the only register read here.

I could not improve on the baseline's 0.80% @ 28/08/2026 and did not override it.

UK RMI demand proxies deliberately NOT carried as a finding. That gap is interesting - it suggests Luceco's core growth is price-led, which the company itself supports ('working with our customers to pass through higher commodity costs', Q1 2026 RNS) - but BMBI measures builders' merchants and Luceco sells through electrical wholesalers and retail, so it is a narrow proxy for a different channel and the lessons file says a proxy like that loses to the company's own number. https://bmbi.co.uk/news-blogs/q2-merchant-sales-down-1-2-year-on-year-prices-rise-5-8-volumes-fall-6-6/

baseline_tension: Mildly against. The baseline's priced_lean_pct of -0.122 is essentially nothing but its components lean negative (short building -0.4, run-up -0.202 against short_squeeze +0.48), and the 20-day run-up of +4.04% and 5-day of +8.41% both say the free control would short this name - my net is +1.4, so I am taking the other side of the control and of a short seller who added into the print. The discount for that is already inside the findings (the run-up finding at -0.4 and the H2-ramp finding cut from -1.0 to -0.7 precisely because it agrees with Saba), which is why the emitted number equals the sum rather than sitting below it; and I have tested the control on this name's own 17 events, where the 5-day run-up ranks at Spearman +0.096 against the print reaction - no predictive power, and the sign is the opposite of the control's assumption.

Added the GBP17.3m six-month net debt build (-0.4) - visible only by putting the FY25 results RNS (GBP52.3m at 31 Dec 2025) next to the July update (GBP69.6m); every English summary repeats the company's own YoY framing.

The English pass had assumed a run-up raises the bar; on this name it does not.

Confirmed the event against the issuer's own financial calendar ('22 September 2026 - 2026 Half year result statement') and confirmed every LUCE results RNS is timestamped 07:00, settling bmo independently of the vendor flag.

Found the departing founder-CEO's 505,000-share sale at 224.06p on 21 August, two days before the 30-day closed period for a 22 September interim would open - carried as corroboration inside the new-CEO finding rather than as a separate finding, to avoid double-counting the transition.
Discovered the FCA aggregated CSV currently publishes staler data than the baseline holds; recorded rather than acted on.

Net effect: impact sum moved +0.5 to +0.1 before the lessons file, expected move +1.5 to +0.5. The domestic pass was net NEGATIVE on the sizing - it added four concrete negatives and one positive - which is the opposite of what a hunter hoping to justify a second pass would want, and is the honest result.
lessons_applied: 'Financing is a question, not a verdict' cut the net-debt finding from -1.0 to -0.4. The money bought inventory explicitly 'ahead of the second half', which corroborates the very H2 ramp the guidance needs, and the FY24-to-FY25 record shows the working capital reversing (adjusted FCF GBP3.5m then GBP30.4m). Checking the reaction history on that line then settled it: at the 2025 interims net debt printed +72.6% YoY and the stock rose 9.46%.

'Positioning is the thing to beat, not the thing to agree with' cut the H2-ramp finding from -1.0 to -0.7 - it restates what a building short seller is already expressing - and raised the short-interest finding from +0.5 to +0.7, since a short that must cover is fuel rather than a warning. It stays small because 0.80% is not crowded.

'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error' and 'the tail is intact, so do not size as if it were not' raised the Demand Flexibility finding from +2.0 to +2.2 and, more importantly, widened its band to [-3.0, +8.0]. With five analysts (the 3-7 band the file says is the unpositioned regime) and a median absolute print move of 4.02% on this name, a narrow band around a small number was the wrong shape.

'Two findings resting on one document are one finding' made me drop the standalone Energy-Transition drop-through finding I had drafted and fold it into the H2-ramp finding, since both rest on the 28 July RNS - and made me declare explicitly in the independence fields that the H2-ramp and net-debt findings are not independent of each other and point opposite ways on the same inventory build.

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series' kept the BMBI/RMI volume divergence out of the findings entirely and into searched_and_found_nothing, because BMBI measures builders' merchants and Luceco sells through electrical wholesalers and retail.

'Keep findings inside the exit window' moved the 27 October Q3 trading update - the first full quarter under the changed mechanics, and the genuinely decisive event - and the new CEO's likely strategic review into outside_window.

Net effect of the file: impact sum +0.1 to +1.4, expected move +0.5 to +1.4. The file moved this hunt materially and in one direction - it cut the negatives that were either priced by the short register or explained by the company, and widened the tail on the one finding with real asymmetry.
